chosen_property.label: participant
chosen_property.justification: participant fits the relation of an event involving entities as participants.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

chosen_property.label: source

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: object

Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: beforeMedia

Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: exceptDate
candidates.comment: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: byMonthDay

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: subjectOf

Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: mentions

Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: lesser
candidates.comment: A lesser ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than the object value. Also called: is less than, is smaller than, falls below. Examples: "Low lesser Medium", "Small lesser Large", "Cold lesser Warm". Distinct from lesserOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: mainEntity

candidates.label: observationAbout

Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: guidelineSubject

Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: associatedArticle

candidates.label: itemReviewed

Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: mentions

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: relevantOccupation
candidates.comment: A relevant occupation relation between a job posting and the specific occupation it describes. Also called job role, occupation type. Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."

relations.definition: Indicates that the subject rivals or contends with the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: competes_with: Indicates that the subject rivals or contends with the object.

Nvidia -> SK Hynix

chosen_property.label: competesWith
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that the subject rivals or contends with the object.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses competition between organizations; minting new property.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: lesserOrEqual
candidates.comment: A lesser or equal ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than or equal to the object value. Also called: is less than or equal to, is at most, does not exceed. Examples: "Low lesserOrEqual Medium", "Small lesserOrEqual Small", "Cold lesserOrEqual Cold". Distinct from lesser, which strictly indicates a smaller value.

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: isSimilarTo
candidates.comment: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

relations.definition: Indicates that the subject became a member or part of the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: joined: Indicates that the subject became a member or part of the object.

instances: SK Hynix -> Nasdaq

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.justification: isPartOf expresses membership in a larger entity.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.
